status_summary: No HHS investigation of medical schools or the ACGME under Coats-Snowe, no opt-in communication to schools and no state-funding condition was found. HHS reorganized its Office for Civil Rights effective 2026-06-28, creating a Conscience and Religious Freedom Division whose listed statutes include the Coats-Snowe Amendment; that is an enforcement structure rather than any of the specific steps. A 2025-12-15 letter from members of Congress asked HHS and CMS to require opt-in abortion training as a condition of federal graduate medical education funding; no HHS response was found.

timeline.event: HHS Office for Civil Rights reorganization took effect (approved 2026-05-14, published 2026-06-30), creating a Conscience and Religious Freedom Division that enforces Coats-Snowe among other conscience laws.

title: Enforce Coats-Snowe in medical education and keep abortion training opt-in
uncertainties: The OCR reorganization notice (91 FR 39626) was re-read in review: approved 2026-05-14, effective 2026-06-28, it lists the Coats-Snowe Amendment (42 U.S.C. 238n) among laws enforced by the Conscience and Religious Freedom Division and does not mention medical schools, the ACGME or abortion training. A Federal Register API term search for Coats-Snowe since 2025-01-20 returned four documents, and a review variant on abortion training returned two: the FY 2027 IPPS final rule (2026-08-04) and the CY 2026 OPPS final rule (2025-11-25). Their search excerpts show commenters on the graduate medical education nondiscrimination provisions asking CMS to require opt-in abortion training in place of the ACGME opt-out model; the agency responses fall in portions of the rules that were not read (federalregister.gov pages are cut short), so whether CMS adopted, deferred or declined that request is unverified. On the congressional side, a medical society letter of 2025-10-10 describes Sec. 237 of the House FY 2026 Labor-HHS bill (H.R. 5304, reported 2025-09-11 and left on the Union Calendar) as conditioning training-program funds on opt-in abortion training; whether any such provision is in Division B of the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026 (Public Law 119-75, enacted 2026-02-03) could not be checked because the govinfo.gov text is cut short before that division. A secondary bill page describes a similar opt-in provision in the House FY 2027 Labor-HHS bill (H.R. 9260, reported 2026-06-11, on the Union Calendar per its govinfo status record); the bill text on govinfo.gov is also cut short and the provision was not read. The 2025-12-15 congressional letter and a 2026-03-16 press interview in which the Assistant Secretary for Health urged students to refuse procedures they object to are not HHS actions and are not in the timeline. HHS OCR press pages and non-public enforcement activity were not checked.
